question.text: What should a driver do with their eyes and following distance on the interstate?

answer.text: On the interstate keep your eyes moving to know what is happening around you, check the mirrors often, and avoid tailgating by using the four second rule with extra space on wet or slippery roads.

teaching.text: In short, on the interstate keep your eyes moving to know what is happening around you, check the mirrors often, and avoid tailgating by using the four second rule with extra space on wet or slippery roads. The hook to keep is: Eyes moving, four seconds.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On the interstate keep your eyes moving to know what is happening around you, check the mirrors often, and avoid tailgating by using the four second rule with extra space on wet or slippery roads.

question.text: How should lane changes and speed changes be made on the interstate?

answer.text: Let other drivers know what you will do before you do it, never slow down or change lanes suddenly, treat frequent lane changes as unsafe, and before changing lanes or passing check the mirrors, signal and check the blind spot on the side you will move to.

teaching.text: In short, let other drivers know what you will do before you do it, never slow down or change lanes suddenly, treat frequent lane changes as unsafe, and before changing lanes or passing check the mirrors, signal and check the blind spot on the side you will move to. The hook to keep is: Signal early, no sudden moves.

question.text: When may a driver stop on an interstate, and how is help signaled?

answer.text: Never stop in an interstate traffic lane; stopping on an interstate is illegal except in an emergency, and then you move into the breakdown lane as far right as possible, raise the hood, tie a white cloth on the vehicle and stay inside if you need help.

teaching.text: In short, never stop in an interstate traffic lane; stopping on an interstate is illegal except in an emergency, and then you move into the breakdown lane as far right as possible, raise the hood, tie a white cloth on the vehicle and stay inside if you need help. The hook to keep is: Stopping only for emergencies.

question.text: Which lane should a driver use on the interstate?

answer.text: Drive in the right lane of the interstate unless you are passing another vehicle or a sign directs otherwise.

teaching.text: In short, drive in the right lane of the interstate unless you are passing another vehicle or a sign directs otherwise. The hook to keep is: Keep right except to pass.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Drive in the right lane of the interstate unless you are passing another vehicle or a sign directs otherwise.

question.text: What does the handbook say about fatigue on interstates?

answer.text: Do not drive when tired, since fatigue is a major cause of interstate crashes, and if you become tired stop and rest in a safe area as soon as possible.

teaching.text: In short, do not drive when tired, since fatigue is a major cause of interstate crashes, and if you become tired stop and rest in a safe area as soon as possible. The hook to keep is: Do not drive tired.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not drive when tired, since fatigue is a major cause of interstate crashes, and if you become tired stop and rest in a safe area as soon as possible.

question.text: What should a driver do after missing an exit?

answer.text: If you miss your exit never stop and back up and never use the emergency turnaround, which is reserved for emergency and maintenance vehicles; go on to the next exit.

teaching.text: In short, if you miss your exit never stop and back up and never use the emergency turnaround, which is reserved for emergency and maintenance vehicles; go on to the next exit. The hook to keep is: If you miss your exit.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you miss your exit never stop and back up and never use the emergency turnaround, which is reserved for emergency and maintenance vehicles; go on to the next exit.

question.text: How does handling a missed exit differ from an emergency stop?

answer.text: A missed exit is handled by continuing to the next one, never by backing up on the interstate and never by using the emergency crossover.

teaching.text: In short, a missed exit is handled by continuing to the next one, never by backing up on the interstate and never by using the emergency crossover. The hook to keep is: Missed exit versus emergency stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A missed exit is handled by continuing to the next one, never by backing up on the interstate and never by using the emergency crossover.

question.text: When should cruise control never be used?

answer.text: Never use cruise control in conditions such as rain, fog, snow or ice.

teaching.text: In short, never use cruise control in conditions such as rain, fog, snow or ice. The hook to keep is: No cruise control in bad weather.

question.text: What must a driver do when approaching a stopped emergency or repair vehicle with flashing lights?

answer.text: When a police, emergency or repair vehicle sits at the roadside with a flashing light, you must slow down, continue with caution and move a lane away from it as soon as that is safe, and if no lane change is possible you must pass at twenty miles per hour under the speed limit.

teaching.text: In short, when a police, emergency or repair vehicle sits at the roadside with a flashing light, you must slow down, continue with caution and move a lane away from it as soon as that is safe, and if no lane change is possible you must pass at twenty miles per hour under the speed limit. The hook to keep is: Stopped emergency vehicles on the interstate.

question.text: On the interstate, when does the twenty mile per hour slowdown rule apply instead of a lane change?

answer.text: Passing a stopped emergency vehicle on the interstate requires a lane change where safe, and only when no lane change is possible does the rule become slowing to twenty miles per hour under the limit.

teaching.text: In short, passing a stopped emergency vehicle on the interstate requires a lane change where safe, and only when no lane change is possible does the rule become slowing to twenty miles per hour under the limit. The hook to keep is: Move over first, slow as fallback.

question.text: What steps does a driver take to pass a vehicle or bicycle?

answer.text: To pass a vehicle or bicycle ahead, make sure you have enough distance, signal left, look to the rear in the mirrors and over your left shoulder to check whether you are being passed, then change lanes and pass on the left.

teaching.text: In short, to pass a vehicle or bicycle ahead, make sure you have enough distance, signal left, look to the rear in the mirrors and over your left shoulder to check whether you are being passed, then change lanes and pass on the left. The hook to keep is: How to pass on the left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: To pass a vehicle or bicycle ahead, make sure you have enough distance, signal left, look to the rear in the mirrors and over your left shoulder to check whether you are being passed, then change lanes and pass on the left.

question.text: How much clearance is required when passing, and when may you return to the right?

answer.text: Overtake vehicles and bicycles on the left with at least four feet of clearance, stay out until the whole front of the vehicle or the bicyclist shows in your inside rearview mirror, then signal right, glance over your right shoulder at the blind spot and move back to the right.

teaching.text: In short, overtake vehicles and bicycles on the left with at least four feet of clearance, stay out until the whole front of the vehicle or the bicyclist shows in your inside rearview mirror, then signal right, glance over your right shoulder at the blind spot and move back to the right. The hook to keep is: Four feet and the mirror check.

question.text: What should a driver do when another vehicle is passing?

answer.text: When another vehicle is passing you, slow a little and keep right so the other driver can pass more safely.

teaching.text: In short, when another vehicle is passing you, slow a little and keep right so the other driver can pass more safely. The hook to keep is: When you are being passed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When another vehicle is passing you, slow a little and keep right so the other driver can pass more safely.

question.text: When may a driver pass on the right?

answer.text: A driver may pass on the right on a multilane road, and on other roads may pass on the right of a vehicle or bicycle that is turning or preparing to turn left when there is room to go by safely.

teaching.text: In short, a driver may pass on the right on a multilane road, and on other roads may pass on the right of a vehicle or bicycle that is turning or preparing to turn left when there is room to go by safely. The hook to keep is: When passing on the right is.

question.text: When is passing on the right lawful, and when is it never allowed?

answer.text: Passing on the right is lawful on a multilane road or beside a vehicle turning left, but never by leaving the pavement or the main traveled part of the road.

teaching.text: In short, passing on the right is lawful on a multilane road or beside a vehicle turning left, but never by leaving the pavement or the main traveled part of the road. The hook to keep is: Lawful right pass versus shoulder pass.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Passing on the right is lawful on a multilane road or beside a vehicle turning left, but never by leaving the pavement or the main traveled part of the road.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Lawful right pass versus shoulder pass

question.text: May a vehicle ever be passed by driving off the pavement?

answer.text: Under no conditions may a vehicle be passed by driving off the pavement or off the main traveled part of the road.

teaching.text: In short, under no conditions may a vehicle be passed by driving off the pavement or off the main traveled part of the road. The hook to keep is: Never pass on the shoulder.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Under no conditions may a vehicle be passed by driving off the pavement or off the main traveled part of the road.

question.text: At which locations must a driver never pass?

answer.text: Do not pass on hills, on curves, at railroad crossings, at intersections or where a changed path ahead sign appears.

teaching.text: In short, do not pass on hills, on curves, at railroad crossings, at intersections or where a changed path ahead sign appears. The hook to keep is: Where never to pass.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Do not pass on hills, on curves, at railroad crossings, at intersections or where a changed path ahead sign appears.

question.text: What are interstates, and by what other names are they known?

answer.text: Interstates are multiple lane divided roads built for high speed travel, known elsewhere as expressways, throughways, turnpikes, toll roads, limited access highways or freeways, some free and some tolled.

teaching.text: In short, interstates are multiple lane divided roads built for high speed travel, known elsewhere as expressways, throughways, turnpikes, toll roads, limited access highways or freeways, some free and some tolled. The hook to keep is: What interstates are.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Interstates are multiple lane divided roads built for high speed travel, known elsewhere as expressways, throughways, turnpikes, toll roads, limited access highways or freeways, some free and some tolled.

question.text: What advantages do interstates offer, and why learn to use them properly?

answer.text: Interstates are multi lane, controlled access roads on which you can drive very long distances without interruption, designed for quicker and safer travel, so learning to use them properly matters.

teaching.text: In short, interstates are multi lane, controlled access roads on which you can drive very long distances without interruption, designed for quicker and safer travel, so learning to use them properly matters. The hook to keep is: Controlled access roads.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Interstates are multi lane, controlled access roads on which you can drive very long distances without interruption, designed for quicker and safer travel, so learning to use them properly matters.

question.text: What are speed change lanes for?

answer.text: Speed change lanes run alongside the interstate for a short distance to connect entrance or exit ramps with the travel lanes and let vehicles speed up or slow down when entering or leaving.

teaching.text: In short, speed change lanes run alongside the interstate for a short distance to connect entrance or exit ramps with the travel lanes and let vehicles speed up or slow down when entering or leaving. The hook to keep is: Speed change lanes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Speed change lanes run alongside the interstate for a short distance to connect entrance or exit ramps with the travel lanes and let vehicles speed up or slow down when entering or leaving.

question.text: What steps does a driver take on the entrance ramp and acceleration lane?

answer.text: An entrance ramp is a short one way road onto the interstate that leads to the acceleration lane, where you stay right, signal left, speed up to interstate speed, check the blind spot over the left shoulder and change lanes when the travel lane is safe.

teaching.text: In short, an entrance ramp is a short one way road onto the interstate that leads to the acceleration lane, where you stay right, signal left, speed up to interstate speed, check the blind spot over the left shoulder and change lanes when the travel lane is safe. The hook to keep is: Using the entrance ramp.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An entrance ramp is a short one way road onto the interstate that leads to the acceleration lane, where you stay right, signal left, speed up to interstate speed, check the blind spot over the left shoulder and change lanes when the travel lane is safe.

question.text: How do the entrance ramp and exit ramp procedures differ?

answer.text: On an entrance ramp the entering driver speeds up and yields to interstate traffic, while on an exit ramp the driver slows only after reaching the deceleration lane.

teaching.text: In short, on an entrance ramp the entering driver speeds up and yields to interstate traffic, while on an exit ramp the driver slows only after reaching the deceleration lane. The hook to keep is: Acceleration versus deceleration lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On an entrance ramp the entering driver speeds up and yields to interstate traffic, while on an exit ramp the driver slows only after reaching the deceleration lane.

question.text: Who yields when entering the interstate?

answer.text: A driver entering the interstate must yield to drivers already on it.

teaching.text: In short, a driver entering the interstate must yield to drivers already on it. The hook to keep is: Entering traffic yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A driver entering the interstate must yield to drivers already on it.

question.text: How does a driver leave the interstate?

answer.text: An exit ramp is a short one way road connecting the interstate to another road, and to leave you signal for a lane change, move into the deceleration lane nearest the exit and slow to the posted exit speed.

teaching.text: In short, an exit ramp is a short one way road connecting the interstate to another road, and to leave you signal for a lane change, move into the deceleration lane nearest the exit and slow to the posted exit speed. The hook to keep is: Using the exit ramp.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: An exit ramp is a short one way road connecting the interstate to another road, and to leave you signal for a lane change, move into the deceleration lane nearest the exit and slow to the posted exit speed.

question.text: Where should a driver look to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights?

answer.text: To avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights look ahead toward the right edge of the highway until the bright lights pass and your vision returns, a habit that also helps you spot bicyclists or pedestrians near the road edge.

teaching.text: In short, to avoid being blinded by oncoming headlights look ahead toward the right edge of the highway until the bright lights pass and your vision returns, a habit that also helps you spot bicyclists or pedestrians near the road edge. question.text: What winter hazards do interstates and their ramps present?

answer.text: Icy and snow covered interstates and their ramps are very dangerous, so slow down and drive with care, remembering that bridges and overpasses may be more slippery than the main road.

question.text: What does a yellow edge line on your right mean on a divided highway?

answer.text: If the edge line to your right on a divided highway is painted yellow you are going the wrong way, because on a divided highway or interstate the line on your right should be white.

teaching.text: In short, if the edge line to your right on a divided highway is painted yellow you are going the wrong way, because on a divided highway or interstate the line on your right should be white. The hook to keep is: Yellow edge line on the right.

question.text: What line colors should be on your right and left on a divided highway?

answer.text: A yellow line on your right on a divided highway warns you are going the wrong way, whereas the correct position puts white on the right and yellow on the left.

teaching.text: In short, a yellow line on your right on a divided highway warns you are going the wrong way, whereas the correct position puts white on the right and yellow on the left. The hook to keep is: Yellow right means wrong way.

question.text: How might a driver warn a vehicle ahead of a pass at night?

answer.text: At night it may be necessary to flick the headlights from low to high to low to warn the driver ahead that you intend to pass.

question.text: What extra care applies when passing while towing a trailer?

answer.text: When passing while towing a trailer be especially sure you are well past the vehicle or bicycle before pulling back into its lane.

teaching.text: In short, when passing while towing a trailer be especially sure you are well past the vehicle or bicycle before pulling back into its lane. The hook to keep is: Passing while towing a trailer.

question.text: What extra care applies when passing with a wide load or wide vehicle?

answer.text: When towing a wide load or driving an unusually wide vehicle be especially careful when passing any motorist or bicyclist.

teaching.text: In short, when towing a wide load or driving an unusually wide vehicle be especially careful when passing any motorist or bicyclist. The hook to keep is: Passing with a wide load.
